visible_text: The figure shows a region bounded by the lines y = 3, y = x + 3, and y = 6 – 2x. Which of the following inequalities are true for any point (h, k) in the shaded region? I. k ≥ 3; II. h – k ≥ –3; III. 2h + k ≤ 6. Options: A: I only; B: II only; C: I and II only; D: I, II and III.
reasoning: The three boundary lines of the shaded region give exactly the three inequalities: the horizontal line y = 3 yields k ≥ 3 (statement I); the line y = x + 3 yields k ≤ h + 3, which rearranges to h – k ≥ –3 (statement II); and the line y = 6 – 2x yields k ≤ 6 – 2h, which rearranges to 2h + k ≤ 6 (statement III). All three hold for the entire shaded region, so the correct choice is D.
